analysis: The only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md is one added table row (head line 572) in the `darkbloom benchmark` section. It documents a `--prompt-prep` benchmark mode with `--prompt-prep-lengths` and `--iterations`. The row describes it as CPU-only and tokenizer-only, timing prompt preparation and exiting 2 on token-ID or decoded-field differences. This is documentation only, with no code, config, key handling, protocol or authorization change. I found no security regression against the supplied threat model, including TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, T-041 and the App Attest entries. The row does not touch the encrypted prefix cache, attestation, coordinator authorization or logout/revocation behavior (A-008, T-053). The documented mode loads no model weights and makes no network calls, so it adds no new asset exposure. Unverified contract: the referenced implementation in `provider-swift/Sources/ProviderBenchmark/PromptPreparationBenchmark.swift` was not supplied. I did not confirm its tokenizer-only and CPU-only claims, whether it logs prompt content, or whether any benchmark input is persisted. If that file is part of this PR, a code-level pass should check that it handles no real consumer prompts (A-001) and writes no plaintext to disk or logs. The rest of the supplied file text is unchanged surrounding documentation, and I did not treat it as new behavior.
